thread:
alex: Quick update from staging run — I spun up a decoupled prefill + decode queue config and enabled phase-aware token budgets. Wanted to share the microbench before we ship any scheduler changes.

alex: TL;DR: p50 gen latency down ~12% for long-chat flows, throughput up ~9% under steady state, but p99 for short prefill-heavy calls jumped ~4%. KV hit-rate dipped slightly (−6%) during cold spikes.

jamie: can you paste the dashboard or numbers? link pls

alex: Dashboard: https://staging-perf/redwood/exp/decouple-248123. Key numbers: 
```
config: {
  queue_policy: "phase_separate",
  prefill_token_budget: 80,
  decode_token_budget: 24,
  phase_precedence: "prefill-first-on-short-queues",
  kv_warmup_ms: 120
}
p50_latency_long = 120ms -> 106ms
p99_latency_short = 18ms -> 18.7ms
kv_hit_rate_overall = 0.82 -> 0.77
cpu_util = 64% -> 70% (after change)
```

perf-bot: benchmark job finished: run/248123. Summary: throughput +9%, median latency -12%, tail +4% on short sequences. Attachments: /artifacts/248123/trace.tar.gz

vijay: did you confirm KV working set eviction wasn't the culprit for the hit-rate dip?

alex: dug in: eviction counts spiked for some GPUs during warmup windows. Looks like our prefill bursts cause KV churn because we push more simultaneous prefill requests into the cache warmup path. Sample log: `kv_evictions=312, kv_warmups=540` during a 10s window.

emily: i suspect the kernel selector is switching to the larger attention kernel for mixed sequence lengths during the handoff — that can blow tail on short calls. any selector traces?

alex: yes, saw a few kernel handoffs logged. Relevant snippet from trace: `kernel_switch: attn_small->attn_blocked @ seq=64` which corresponds with decode ramp. I think the sizing heuristic uses aggregate batch length which is skewed by prefill-heavy items.

jamie: simple mitigation idea: split token budget so prefill_max_tokens=48 and decode_min_tokens=8, plus prefer kernel affinity for sequences <64 for the first decode window. worth trying?

alex: will try a conservative tweak: `prefill_token_budget=48, decode_token_budget=32, kernel_affinity_short=true`. I'll run a 2h A/B against current and capture KV cold-hit scenarios.

vijay: can we also add a KV gating step: if kv_hit_rate < 0.6 then throttle prefill bursters to allow warms? probably a short circuit to avoid thrash.

emily: also add a regression test in CI that simulates N cold clients joining simultaneously (N=80) to catch KV churn regressions.

alex: ack — test and A/B in progress. Rollback plan: if p99_short increases >5% or overall kv_hit_rate < 0.7 we flip `queue_policy=single` and revert budgets.

jamie: sgtm. tag me when you have the AB results. :white_check_mark:

emily: nice writeup — also file a perf regression ticket if the A/B shows any tail regressions.

alex: will do, dropping logs & traces into the ticket. thanks all.
